A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SoundMind research. Their complete text, equations, tables and figures are readable. v1 has no appendices; v2 adds Appendices A–D. Dataset and algorithm renaming can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset statistics and model evaluations across audio-to-text, text-to-audio and audio-to-audio reasoning in Tables 3–6.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds reward ablation results in Table 7 and a qualitative account of a human-listening TTS comparison in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The proposed system retains Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, the same format, correctness and length rewards, and the REINFORCE++ objective. SoundMind-RL is a rename of the algorithm. Newly evaluated reward ablations do not replace the full proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix B adds evaluation of speech-synthesis quality on representative dataset samples, supplementing the logical-inference evaluations. The underlying 6,446-sample dataset and three reasoning modality configurations remain unchanged. Appendix C's potential applications are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Appendix B newly compares the retained MegaTTS-3 synthesis component with WhisperSpeech, Spark-TTS and Zonos. The reasoning comparator sets in Tables 4–6 are unchanged; Appendix A merely expands their descriptions.

E3.justification: Main-experiment splits, metrics, training budget and reward weights remain unchanged. Added evaluations introduce reward configurations in Table 7 and representative-sample human listening in Appendix B. Notably, the configuration without text rewards also increases both remaining audio reward weights to 1.0.

E4.justification: v1 contains no reward-component ablations. Appendix D and Table 7 add direct tests of configurations without audio, text or answer rewards, substantially expanding evidence about the reward design. Appendix B also adds a reported comparative analysis supporting the TTS engine selection.

E5.justification: Appendix B newly reports multi-rater assessment summarized through mean opinion scores. This adds a human-rating aggregation practice, but numerical scores, rater counts and uncertainty are not supplied. Run counts, seeds, confidence intervals and significance tests remain unreported.

E6.justification: The original benchmark values in Tables 4–6 are unchanged. Table 7 adds accuracies of 70.82%, 48.84% and 60.24% for configurations without audio, text and answer rewards, respectively, versus 81.40% for the full configuration. Appendix B newly reports MegaTTS-3 as having the highest mean opinion scores, without numerical values.

T1.justification: The reward definitions, clipped policy objective, advantage normalization and KL expression in Equations 1–7 are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs, and the new appendix interpretations are empirical rather than formal derivations.

C1.justification: The dataset and RL contributions remain intact. The abstract more explicitly confines comparative performance claims to the SoundMind benchmark. The dataset priority claim is also qualified from the first open-source resource of its kind to among the first in Section 2.

C2.justification: The limitations expand beyond a brief WER caveat to reward rigidity, uncertain generalization to open-ended tasks, and synthetic-speech and automatic-annotation artifacts. Appendix D adds interpretations of reward-component roles. Section 5.3 gives more specific explanations for increased WER, including longer generations and absent fluency constraints.

D1.justification: v2 adds a direct Hugging Face dataset link in the front matter and explicit reward-weight configurations for the new ablations. Main training hardware, budget, full-model weights and the GitHub access information are retained. The added TTS study description lacks detailed reproduction settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning reasoning, synthetic speech, TTS alternatives and potential applications, and removes the s1 reference. It softens the dataset priority claim to among the first. The central positioning relative to Logic-RL and existing audio reasoning research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, dataset discussion and results narrative undergo extensive rewriting. ALR becomes the task name, SoundMind the dataset name, and SoundMind-RL the algorithm name. Results gain numbered modality-specific subsections, and four appendices extend the document structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds the ablation table, expands captions, updates figure labels and rearranges existing displays, including Table 2 and Figure 3. The original diagrams, example, duration histograms and benchmark table structures remain largely intact.

improvement.justification: The added ablations partially address v1's lack of component-level validation, while expanded limitations give a more candid account of applicability and synthetic-data concerns. These are useful gains, but the TTS comparison lacks numerical scores and study counts, and the no-text ablation also changes audio weights, weakening isolated attribution. The core benchmark results remain unchanged.
